findings.title: The plot card does not show the waiting list

location.description: the open plot 3 tile in the Elm Row plot card, top right of the hero on desktop and widescreen, below the button on phone and tablet

findings.viewer_experience: A coordinator sees what a spreadsheet already shows, which plots are free. They do not see what makes Plotwise different: an open plot goes to the next person in line.

current.value: plots 3 and 8 are plain green tiles with no person tied to them

findings.target: plot 3 or 8 is tied to the person it is being offered to, inside the same Elm Row example. The maker must supply that person's details; they are not invented here.
findings.fix_direction: Tie plot 3 or 8 to the person it is being offered to, in the same Elm Row example. The maker must supply the details of that person.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen images, a fresh critic sees plot 3 or 8 of the Elm Row card tied to the person it is being offered to.

findings.title: The week and March lines read as fixed rules

location.description: the Plot offers card text 'has a week to say yes'; the Rent reminders card has the matching 'rent is due in March' line

findings.viewer_experience: A coordinator whose garden gives two weeks, or collects rent in April, may decide Plotwise does not fit them.

current.value: 'has a week to say yes' and 'rent is due in March' are unqualified

findings.target: each line is marked as either the example garden's setting or a product rule. Only the maker knows which is true, so the maker must say which.
findings.fix_direction: Mark each line as either the example garden's setting or a product rule. The maker must say which is true for each line.

closed_when.check: In the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen images, a fresh critic sees the Plot offers and Rent reminders lines marked as an example garden's setting or as a product rule.

findings.title: The phone headline ends its lines on 'for' and 'without'

location.description: the headline at the top of the phone hero, breaking as 'Run the waiting list for / your garden without / the spreadsheet'

findings.viewer_experience: The lines end on 'for' and 'without', so the headline does not read in whole phrases as it does on desktop.
findings.target: the phone headline uses the same phrase breaks as desktop: 'Run the waiting list / for your garden / without the spreadsheet', or wraps at the phrases.
findings.fix_direction: Use the same phrase breaks as desktop, or let the headline wrap at the phrases.

closed_when.check: In the phone image, a fresh critic sees the headline lines break at the phrases and not end on 'for' or 'without'.
